- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast increase at 1.5x recent 7-day average growth.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical 30-day mean if deviation > 3σ.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in low-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment < -0.3 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a downtrend, model may lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
